title: Accounts Assistant
description:
If you want a job where you'll actually get to do more than one thing, this could be worth a look.

This is a broad role, you won't spend five days a week doing nothing but processing invoices or chasing the same spreadsheet around.

What will you be doing?

It's a varied Accounts Assistant role, giving you exposure to several areas of the finance function rather than keeping you focused on just one.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing and allocating cash receipts to customer accounts
- Completing bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies
- Managing the sales ledger and ensuring accounts are accurate and up to date
- Supporting credit control, chasing overdue invoices and resolving customer queries
- Processing supplier invoices and preparing regular AP payment runs
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving any differences
- Assisting with the preparation and submission of VAT returns
- Supporting month-end processes and the wider finance team as required

What are they looking for?

You don't need to be the finished article.

You'll probably have worked in an accounts or finance role already and have a reasonable understanding of how a finance department works.

Maybe you're an Accounts Assistant who wants more variety, or perhaps you've spent most of your time in purchase ledger, sales ledger or credit control and you're ready to broaden your experience.

Either way, you'll need to be comfortable with numbers, reasonably handy with Excel and the sort of person who notices when something doesn't look right rather than assuming somebody else will sort it.

Most importantly, you'll be keen to learn.

Why consider it?

You'll get exposure to different areas of finance, work alongside people you can learn from and have the opportunity to take on more responsibility as you develop.

What else?
- Hybrid and flexible working
- 25 days annual leave + bank holidays
- Various employee benefits / retail discounts

So, if your current role has started to feel a bit repetitive or you're simply ready for the next step, click apply now.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Job Title: Bookkeeper (Full-Time or Part-Time)
Location: Central Leeds - Office-Based
Salary: £27,000 - £33,000 per annum (pro-rata for part-time) dependent on experience
Working Hours: Full-time (37 hours per week) or Part-time options available

About the Role
A well-established, independent accountancy practice based in central Leeds is seeking an experienced Bookkeeper to join their team on a full-time or part-time basis. This is an entirely office-based role, ideal for someone who thrives in a vibrant, collaborative practice environment and enjoys direct contact with clients and colleagues.

Key Responsibilities
Maintain accurate double-entry bookkeeping records for a varied portfolio of sole traders, partnerships, and limited companies.
Prepare and submit quarterly VAT returns and EC Sales lists in line with Making Tax Digital (MTD) guidelines.
Carry out regular bank, credit card, and supplier reconciliations.
Process sales and purchase ledgers using cloud accounting platforms (Xero, QuickBooks, Sage).
Post month-end journals, prepayments, and accruals.
Liaise with internal tax and accounts teams to ensure smooth data handover for statutory year-end preparation.

Requirements
Proven track record in bookkeeping within an accountancy practice or bureau environment.
AAT qualified (Level 3 or 4) or Qualified by Experience (QBE).
Practical experience using cloud accounting software (Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage 50).
Sound knowledge of UK VAT regulations and standard accounting practices.
High attention to detail, strong organizational abilities, and clear communication skills.

Package & Benefits
Salary: £27,000 - £33,000 FTE, depending on experience.
Working Pattern: Fully office-based in central Leeds, with flexible start and finish times to assist with travel and personal commitments.
Annual Leave: 23 days holiday, plus 8 bank holidays, plus 1 extra pre-determined day at Christmas.
Pension: Company pension scheme with employer contribution up to 5%.
Professional Fees: Full reimbursement for relevant professional membership fees.
Development: Opportunities for ongoing professional development and training.

title: Interim Finance Officer
description:
Interim Finance Officer

Location: Bradford
Salary: £28,000 - £33,000 per annum, depending on experience
Contract: 6-month fixed-term contract, with potential to become permanent
Hours: Full-time, 1 day a week in the office

We are recruiting for a Finance Officer to join a busy finance team in Bradford on an initial six-month fixed-term contract, with the potential for the role to become permanent for the right person.

This is a varied finance position covering accounts payable, accounts receivable and general ledger activities, making it an excellent opportunity for either an experienced Finance Officer or a high-potential junior finance professional looking to develop their career.

The Role

Working as part of the finance team, you will support a broad range of day-to-day financial processes and help ensure transactions are processed accurately and efficiently.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing accounts payable and accounts receivable transactions.
- Supporting general ledger activities and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Preparing and processing payment runs.
- Completing bank and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Assisting with double-entry bookkeeping.
- Uploading and processing housing benefit schedules.
- Supporting the wider finance team with day-to-day accounting requirements.
- Investigating and resolving financial queries where required.
- Ensuring financial information is accurate, complete and processed within agreed timescales.
- Contributing to the ongoing improvement of finance processes and systems.

About You

We are open to considering candidates at different stages of their finance career.

We're particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate:
- Experience within a finance administration, accounts or Finance Officer position.
- Exposure to accounts payable and/or accounts receivable.
- Good knowledge of Excel and confidence working with financial data.
- Ideally, experience using Excel lookups and pivot tables, or the aptitude to develop these skills quickly.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- The initiative to identify issues and find solutions rather than simply follow processes.
- A proactive and collaborative approach to working.

Experience within the housing sector would be advantageous, as would experience of HomeMaster, although neither is essential.

The Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking for a role that offers both variety and development.

For a junior candidate, the position provides the opportunity to broaden your experience across AP, AR and general ledger functions while developing your technical finance skills.

For a more experienced Finance Officer, the role offers the opportunity to take ownership of a varied workload and use your existing systems and process knowledge to make an immediate contribution.

The initial contract is for six months, with the potential for the position to become permanent for the successful candidate.

If you're an ambitious junior finance professional or an experienced Finance Officer looking for your next opportunity in Bradford, we'd be keen to hear from you.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Payroll Assistant

Bradford / Keighley area

Up to £35k depending on experience

Full Time - Permanent

Hybrid, up to 2 days at home

A long-standing and well-established accountancy firm with a strong local presence is looking to add a Payroll Assistant to its Bradford-based team.

This is a smaller, personable team where experience, support and collaboration genuinely go hand in hand. You won't just be another payroll number here, you'll be part of a team that shares knowledge, supports one another and takes pride in delivering a high-quality service to its clients. There's also free on-site parking, making those office days a little easier!

You'll manage your own portfolio of clients from start to finish, working across different payroll frequencies, employee numbers, processes and client requirements. Some payrolls are relatively small, with around 15 employees, while others can be up to around 200 employees. You'll therefore need to be organised, adaptable and comfortable managing competing deadlines, while also keeping an accurate record of your time.

Ideally, you'll have gained your payroll experience within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or similar multi-client environment. This type of background will give you a good understanding of managing several clients simultaneously, working to different deadlines and adapting your approach depending on the individual client's requirements. However, industry payroll experience will absolutely be considered.

If you've worked in an in-house payroll role but are now looking to move into a practice/bureau environment, we'd be keen to hear from you. The key is being able to demonstrate that you understand the differences between an in-house and client payroll environment - particularly the variety of payrolls, increased deadlines, client communication, time management and the need to regularly switch between different processes and requirements.

You'll need to be someone who is keen to learn, adaptable and genuinely interested in making the move into practice payroll, rather than simply looking for a change of scenery. If you can demonstrate that you'll pick up the multi-client side of the role quickly and enjoy the variety that comes with it, your industry background could be a really strong foundation.

Why this role stands out:
- Join a smaller, friendly and supportive accountancy practice where you'll be known and valued
- Work alongside experienced payroll professionals who are happy to share their knowledge and support your development
- Free on-site parking
- Flexible working hours to suit your lifestyle, for example, 8-4, 9-5, 10-6 or something in between
- Hybrid working available
- Take ownership of your own portfolio of clients
- Build strong, long-term relationships with a varied client base
- Variety across multiple payrolls, industries, processes and deadlines
- Exposure to payrolls ranging from approximately 15 to 200 employees
- Opportunity for overtime or time off in lieu during particularly busy periods
- A role where there is scope to develop your payroll knowledge and broaden your experience

What you'll be doing:
- Running end-to-end payrolls for your own portfolio of clients
- Processing weekly, monthly and mixed-frequency payrolls
- Setting up new payrolls and workplace pension schemes
- Liaising with clients to obtain payroll information and ensure deadlines are met
- Processing and checking BACS payments
- Completing payroll calculations and checking payrolls thoroughly before submission
- Supporting clients and employees with payroll queries, including tax codes, SSP, SMP, holiday pay and other payroll-related matters
- Managing different client requirements and adapting processes where necessary
- Interpreting payroll information and data provided in different formats
- Ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and within agreed timescales
- Keeping on top of your workload and recording time accurately across your client portfolio
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes, templates and reporting
- Working closely with the wider payroll and accounts team, particularly during busy periods
- Keeping up to date with relevant payroll legislation and ensuring processes remain compliant

What we're looking for:
- Previous experience processing payroll, ideally within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or multi-client environment
- Industry payroll experience will be considered where you can demonstrate an understanding of the differences between in-house and practice payroll and a genuine desire to make that transition
- A willingness and ability to learn quickly and adapt to working across multiple clients
- Experience managing payroll from start to finish
- Good knowledge of areas including SSP, SMP, holiday pay, tax codes and workplace pensions
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple deadlines simultaneously
- Comfortable switching between different clients, payrolls and processes without losing sight of detail
- Confident communicating with clients and dealing with payroll queries professionally
- Good time management, including the ability to accurately record and manage time across different clients
- A proactive approach and willingness to get stuck in and support colleagues when workloads increase
- Experience using payroll software, Sage Payroll and/or Xero Payroll experience would be advantageous

This is a great opportunity for an experienced payroll professional who enjoys variety, responsibility and working with clients, and wants to be part of a genuinely supportive practice environment.

Whether you're already working within a practice/bureau and looking for your next move, or you're currently in industry and are keen to make the transition into client payroll, the key is having the right attitude, solid payroll knowledge and the ability to adapt to a more varied, deadline-driven environment.
